questions.stem: Calculate number of molecules present in 5.4 g of urea (Molar mass of urea $= 60\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$)
questions.solution:
Step 1: Moles of urea $n = \frac{m}{M} = \frac{5.4}{60} = 0.09\ \mathrm{mol}$
Step 2: Number of molecules $= n \times N_A = 0.09 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23}$
Step 3: $= 0.54198 \times 10^{23} = 5.419 \times 10^{22}$
Final Answer: (B) $5.419 \times 10^{22}$
Quick Tip: Molecules = (mass / molar mass) $\times N_A$; keep track of the power of ten when the mole number is below 1.

questions.stem: The common name of Benzene-1,2-diol is
questions.solution:
Step 1: The three benzenediols have common names: 1,2- (ortho) is catechol, 1,3- (meta) is resorcinol and 1,4- (para) is quinol (hydroquinone). Pyrogallol is benzene-1,2,3-triol.
Step 2: Benzene-1,2-diol has the two $\mathrm{-OH}$ groups ortho to each other, so it is catechol.
Final Answer: (A) Catechol
Quick Tip: Remember the order o, m, p = Catechol, Resorcinol, Quinol (C-R-Q).

questions.stem: The solubility product of salt $\mathrm{B_2A}$ is $3.2 \times 10^{-11}$ at 298 K . What is solubility of the salt at same temperature?
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\mathrm{B_2A \rightleftharpoons 2B^{+} + A^{2-}}$; if solubility is $S$, then $[\mathrm{B^+}] = 2S$ and $[\mathrm{A^{2-}}] = S$.
Step 2: $K_{sp} = (2S)^{2}(S) = 4S^{3} = 3.2 \times 10^{-11}$
Step 3: $S^{3} = 8 \times 10^{-12}$, so $S = 2 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{mol\,dm^{-3}}$
Final Answer: (C) $2.00 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{mol\,dm^{-3}}$
Quick Tip: For $\mathrm{AB_2}$ or $\mathrm{A_2B}$ type salts $K_{sp} = 4S^{3}$.

questions.stem: Identify the product formed when Hex-3-enenitrile is reduced with diisobutylaluminium hydride followed by acid hydrolysis?
questions.solution:
Step 1: DIBAL-H reduces a nitrile only to the imine stage; acid hydrolysis of the imine gives an aldehyde. It does not reduce an isolated $\mathrm{C=C}$ bond.
Step 2: $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH=CHCH_2C\equiv N \xrightarrow[(ii)\ H_3O^+]{(i)\ DIBAL\text{-}H} CH_3CH_2CH=CHCH_2CHO}$, i.e. hex-3-enal.
Final Answer: (C) Hex-3-enal
Quick Tip: DIBAL-H converts $\mathrm{-C\equiv N}$ and esters to $\mathrm{-CHO}$ and leaves $\mathrm{C=C}$ untouched.

questions.stem: Which of the following xenon compound has chlorine pentafluoride like structure?
questions.solution:
Step 1: In $\mathrm{ClF_5}$, Cl has 5 bond pairs and 1 lone pair ($sp^{3}d^{2}$), so the shape is square pyramidal.
Step 2: In $\mathrm{XeOF_4}$, Xe has 5 bonding domains (1 O + 4 F) and 1 lone pair ($sp^{3}d^{2}$), also square pyramidal. ($\mathrm{XeF_4}$ is square planar, $\mathrm{XeF_6}$ distorted octahedral, $\mathrm{XeO_3}$ pyramidal.)
Final Answer: (D) $\mathrm{XeOF_4}$
Quick Tip: 5 bond pairs + 1 lone pair always gives a square pyramid ($\mathrm{ClF_5}$, $\mathrm{BrF_5}$, $\mathrm{IF_5}$, $\mathrm{XeOF_4}$).

questions.stem: Calculate cryoscopic constant of solvent if depression in freezing point of 0.18 m solution of nonvolatile solute is 0.2 K
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\Delta T_f = K_f \cdot m$, so $K_f = \frac{\Delta T_f}{m}$
Step 2: $K_f = \frac{0.2\ \mathrm{K}}{0.18\ \mathrm{mol\,kg^{-1}}}$
Step 3: $K_f = 1.11\ \mathrm{K\,kg\,mol^{-1}}$
Final Answer: (C) $1.11\ \mathrm{K\,kg\,mol^{-1}}$
Quick Tip: Cryoscopic constant = depression produced by a 1 molal solution.

questions.stem: What is the natural source of salicylic acid?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid) gets its name from Salix, the willow tree; willow bark contains salicin, which gives salicylic acid.
Step 2: Salicylic acid is the starting material for aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid).
Final Answer: (B) Willow plant
Quick Tip: Salix (Latin for willow) $\rightarrow$ salicin $\rightarrow$ salicylic acid $\rightarrow$ aspirin.

questions.stem: Calculate the number of unit cells in $1\ \mathrm{cm^{3}}$ of an element if unit cell edge length is $2.0 \times 10^{-8}\ \mathrm{cm}$.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Volume of one unit cell $a^{3} = (2.0 \times 10^{-8}\ \mathrm{cm})^{3} = 8.0 \times 10^{-24}\ \mathrm{cm^{3}}$
Step 2: Number of unit cells $= \frac{1\ \mathrm{cm^{3}}}{8.0 \times 10^{-24}\ \mathrm{cm^{3}}}$
Step 3: $= 0.125 \times 10^{24} = 1.25 \times 10^{23}$
Final Answer: (C) $1.25 \times 10^{23}$
Quick Tip: Number of unit cells = total volume / $a^{3}$; cube the whole edge, including the power of ten.

questions.stem: Identify the carbon atom numbered from $\mathrm{C'_1}$ to $\mathrm{C_5}$ of monosaccharide unit of DNA nucleotide that lacks oxygen atom from -OH group.
questions.solution:
Step 1: The sugar in DNA is 2-deoxy-D-ribose: compared to ribose, the $\mathrm{-OH}$ at $\mathrm{C'_2}$ is replaced by $\mathrm{-H}$.
Step 2: So $\mathrm{C'_2}$ is the carbon that lacks the oxygen atom of an $\mathrm{-OH}$ group ($\mathrm{C'_1}$ carries the base, $\mathrm{C'_3}$ and $\mathrm{C'_5}$ carry the phosphate links).
Final Answer: (B) $\mathrm{C'_2}$
Quick Tip: 'Deoxy' in deoxyribose refers to the missing oxygen at the $2'$ position.

questions.stem: What is the oxidation number of carbon in methanal?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Methanal is $\mathrm{HCHO}$. Take O.N. of H $= +1$ and O $= -2$; let O.N. of C be $x$.
Step 2: $2(+1) + x + (-2) = 0$, so $x = 0$
Final Answer: (C) zero
Quick Tip: Carbon O.N. in one-carbon compounds: $\mathrm{CH_4}$ $-4$, $\mathrm{CH_3OH}$ $-2$, $\mathrm{HCHO}$ 0, $\mathrm{HCOOH}$ +2, $\mathrm{CO_2}$ +4.

questions.stem: Which from following is the most commonly used refrigerant Freon-12?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Freon-12 is $\mathrm{CCl_2F_2}$ (code 12: number of C - 1 = 0, number of H + 1 = 1 so no H, number of F = 2; remaining valencies are Cl).
Step 2: $\mathrm{CCl_2F_2}$ is named dichlorodifluoromethane.
Final Answer: (B) Dichlorodifluoromethane
Quick Tip: For a two-digit Freon number, add 90 to get C, H, F counts: 12 + 90 = 102 gives 1 C, 0 H, 2 F.

questions.stem: Which among the following salts turns red litmus blue in its aqueous solution?
questions.solution:
Step 1: A salt turns red litmus blue only if its solution is basic, i.e. it is a salt of a strong base and a weak acid.
Step 2: $\mathrm{CH_3COONa}$ (from NaOH and $\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$) hydrolyses: $\mathrm{CH_3COO^- + H_2O \rightleftharpoons CH_3COOH + OH^-}$, giving a basic solution. $\mathrm{CuCl_2}$ is acidic and KCl is neutral.
Final Answer: (A) $\mathrm{CH_3-COONa}$
Quick Tip: Strong base + weak acid salt is basic; weak base + strong acid salt is acidic; strong + strong is neutral.

questions.stem:
Identify ' $B$ ' in the following sequence of reactions.
Acetic acid $\xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text{Thionyl chloride}} \mathrm{A} \xrightarrow{\text{Ammonia}} \mathrm{B}$
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\mathrm{CH_3COOH + SOCl_2 \xrightarrow{\Delta} CH_3COCl + SO_2 + HCl}$, so A is acetyl chloride.
Step 2: Ammonolysis of the acid chloride: $\mathrm{CH_3COCl + 2NH_3 \rightarrow CH_3CONH_2 + NH_4Cl}$, so B is acetamide.
Final Answer: (D) Acetamide
Quick Tip: Acetyl chloride is the intermediate A, not the final product B - read which letter is asked.

questions.stem: A container consists mixture of four gases as $5\ \mathrm{g\,H_2}$, $8\ \mathrm{g\,He}$, $50\ \mathrm{g\,CO_2}$ and 20 g Ne at a certain temperature. Which of the following gases exerts minimum partial pressure?
questions.solution:
Step 1: In a mixture, partial pressure $p_i = x_i P_{total}$, so the gas with the fewest moles has the lowest partial pressure.
Step 2: Moles: $\mathrm{H_2} = \frac{5}{2} = 2.5$; He $= \frac{8}{4} = 2$; $\mathrm{CO_2} = \frac{50}{44} = 1.14$; Ne $= \frac{20}{20} = 1.0$
Step 3: Ne has the least number of moles (1.0 mol).
Final Answer: (D) Ne
Quick Tip: Compare moles, not masses - $\mathrm{CO_2}$ has the largest mass but not the fewest moles.

questions.stem: Calculate the work done if 1 mole of certain gas compressed isothermally and reversibly at 300 K from initial pressure $x$ bar to final pressure $2x$ bar $\left[\mathrm{R = 8.314\ J\,K^{-1}\,mol^{-1}}\right]$
questions.solution:
Step 1: For isothermal reversible work, $W = -2.303\,nRT \log\frac{P_1}{P_2}$
Step 2: $W = -2.303 \times 1 \times 8.314 \times 300 \times \log\frac{x}{2x} = 2.303 \times 8.314 \times 300 \times \log 2$
Step 3: $W = 5744.1 \times 0.3010 = 1729\ \mathrm{J} = 1.729\ \mathrm{kJ}$ (positive, work done on the gas)
Final Answer: (A) 1.729 kJ
Quick Tip: Compression gives positive work (done on the system); the magnitude depends only on the pressure ratio.

questions.stem: Which from following compounds has lowest boiling point?
questions.solution:
Step 1: All are straight-chain alcohols with hydrogen bonding; boiling point rises with molar mass because van der Waals forces increase with chain length.
Step 2: Methanol ($\mathrm{CH_3OH}$) has the smallest molar mass, so it has the lowest boiling point (338 K).
Final Answer: (D) Methanol
Quick Tip: In a homologous series, boiling point increases with each added $\mathrm{CH_2}$ group.

questions.stem: Calculate the radius of an atom of an element in pm if it forms bcc unit cell structure having edge length $4.3 \times 10^{-8}\ \mathrm{cm}$.
questions.solution:
Step 1: In bcc, atoms touch along the body diagonal: $\sqrt{3}a = 4r$, so $r = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}a$
Step 2: $a = 4.3 \times 10^{-8}\ \mathrm{cm} = 430\ \mathrm{pm}$
Step 3: $r = \frac{1.732 \times 430}{4} = \frac{744.8}{4} = 186.2\ \mathrm{pm}$
Final Answer: (A) 186.2
Quick Tip: sc: $r = a/2$; bcc: $r = \sqrt{3}a/4$; fcc: $r = a/(2\sqrt{2})$.

questions.stem: Identify acidic amino acid from following list represented by three letter symbols.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Acidic amino acids have an extra $\mathrm{-COOH}$ group in the side chain: aspartic acid (Asp) and glutamic acid (Glu).
Step 2: Arg and Lys have an extra basic group (basic amino acids); Met is neutral.
Final Answer: (D) Asp
Quick Tip: Acidic = Asp, Glu; Basic = Lys, Arg, His.

questions.stem: What is the number of unpaired electrons in f orbitals of lutetium in its +3 oxidation state?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Lu ($Z = 71$): $\mathrm{[Xe]}\,4f^{14}5d^{1}6s^{2}$
Step 2: $\mathrm{Lu^{3+}}$ loses $6s^{2}$ and $5d^{1}$: $\mathrm{[Xe]}\,4f^{14}$ - all seven f orbitals are completely filled.
Step 3: Unpaired f electrons $= 0$
Final Answer: (D) 0 (zero)
Quick Tip: $\mathrm{La^{3+}}$ ($4f^{0}$) and $\mathrm{Lu^{3+}}$ ($4f^{14}$) are the colourless, diamagnetic ends of the lanthanide series.

questions.stem: Which of the following elements has highest electronegativity?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Electronegativity decreases down a group because atomic size increases and the nucleus attracts the bonding pair less strongly.
Step 2: Li is at the top of group 1, so it has the highest electronegativity (Li 1.0 > Na 0.9 > K 0.8 > Rb 0.8).
Final Answer: (A) Li
Quick Tip: Down a group: size up, electronegativity and ionisation enthalpy down.

questions.stem: What is the product obtained when alkene is reacted with cold and dilute alkaline potassium permanganate?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Cold, dilute alkaline $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ (Baeyer's reagent) adds two $\mathrm{-OH}$ groups across the double bond (syn hydroxylation).
Step 2: e.g. $\mathrm{CH_2=CH_2 + H_2O + [O] \xrightarrow{cold,\ dil.\ alk.\ KMnO_4} HOCH_2-CH_2OH}$, a vicinal diol (glycol); the pink colour disappears.
Final Answer: (B) Glycol
Quick Tip: Cold dilute $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ gives diols; hot acidic $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ cleaves the C=C to acids/ketones.

questions.stem:
A complex reaction takes place in following steps.
$\mathrm{NO_2Cl_{(g)} \longrightarrow NO_{2(g)} + Cl_{(g)}}$ (slow)
$\mathrm{NO_2Cl_{(g)} + Cl_{(g)} \longrightarrow NO_{2(g)} + Cl_{2(g)}}$ (fast)
Identify rate law equation for this reaction.
questions.solution:
Step 1: The overall rate is decided by the slowest step (rate-determining step).
Step 2: The slow step is unimolecular: $\mathrm{NO_2Cl \rightarrow NO_2 + Cl}$, so rate $\mathrm{r = k[NO_2Cl]}$ (first order).
Final Answer: (A) $\mathrm{r = k\,[NO_2Cl]}$
Quick Tip: Do not use the overall equation $\mathrm{2NO_2Cl \rightarrow 2NO_2 + Cl_2}$ to write the rate law; use the slow step.

questions.stem: Which among the following has highest boiling point?
questions.solution:
Step 1: The four structures are isomers of $\mathrm{C_4H_9OH}$: (A) butan-1-ol, (B) 2-methylpropan-1-ol, (C) butan-2-ol, (D) 2-methylpropan-2-ol.
Step 2: All form hydrogen bonds; among isomers, branching makes the molecule more compact, reducing surface area and van der Waals forces, so boiling point falls: $1^\circ$ straight chain > branched $1^\circ$ > $2^\circ$ > $3^\circ$.
Step 3: Butan-1-ol (391 K) > 2-methylpropan-1-ol (381 K) > butan-2-ol (373 K) > 2-methylpropan-2-ol (355 K).
Final Answer: (A) Butan-1-ol (straight-chain structure)
Quick Tip: For isomeric alcohols, the unbranched primary alcohol always boils highest.

questions.stem: Which of the following is correct decreasing order of bond length regarding $\mathrm{N_2}$, $\mathrm{O_2}$ and $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ ?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Bond length decreases as bond order increases: $\mathrm{N_2}$ (bond order 3) < $\mathrm{O_2}$ (bond order 2).
Step 2: $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ has a single bond between much larger atoms (3rd period), so it is the longest.
Step 3: Bond lengths: $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ (199 pm) > $\mathrm{O_2}$ (121 pm) > $\mathrm{N_2}$ (110 pm)
Final Answer: (A) $\mathrm{Cl_2 > O_2 > N_2}$
Quick Tip: Higher bond order and smaller atoms both mean a shorter bond.

questions.stem:
Calculate the standard enthalpy change of following reaction.
$\mathrm{CH_{4(g)} + 2O_{2(g)} \rightarrow CO_{2(g)} + 2H_2O_{(\ell)}}$
if $\Delta_f H^\circ\,(\mathrm{CH_4}) = -75\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$
$\Delta_f H^\circ\,(\mathrm{CO_2}) = -390\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$
$\Delta_f H^\circ\,(\mathrm{H_2O}) = -286\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\Delta_r H^\circ = \sum \Delta_f H^\circ(\text{products}) - \sum \Delta_f H^\circ(\text{reactants})$; $\Delta_f H^\circ(\mathrm{O_2}) = 0$
Step 2: $\Delta_r H^\circ = [-390 + 2(-286)] - [-75 + 0]$
Step 3: $= -962 + 75 = -887\ \mathrm{kJ}$
Final Answer: (A) $-887.00\ \mathrm{kJ}$
Quick Tip: Multiply each $\Delta_f H^\circ$ by its stoichiometric coefficient and remember elements have $\Delta_f H^\circ = 0$.

questions.stem: What is reduction potential of hydrogen gas electrode when pure hydrogen gas is at 1 atmospheric pressure and platinum electrode is in contact with HCl solution of pH 1 at 298 K ?
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\mathrm{2H^+ + 2e^- \rightarrow H_2}$; $E = E^\circ - \frac{0.0592}{2}\log\frac{P_{H_2}}{[\mathrm{H^+}]^{2}}$ with $E^\circ = 0$
Step 2: With $P_{H_2} = 1$ atm: $E = -\frac{0.0592}{2} \times 2\log\frac{1}{[\mathrm{H^+}]} = -0.0592\ \mathrm{pH}$
Step 3: $E = -0.0592 \times 1 = -0.0592\ \mathrm{V}$
Final Answer: (B) -0.0592 V
Quick Tip: For a hydrogen electrode at 1 atm and 298 K, $E_{red} = -0.0592\,\mathrm{pH}$.

questions.stem: Identify tertiary amine from following.
questions.solution:
Step 1: A tertiary amine has three carbon groups on nitrogen ($\mathrm{R_3N}$). Cyclohexanamine and ethane-1,2-diamine are $1^\circ$; N-phenylbenzeneamine $\mathrm{(C_6H_5)_2NH}$ is $2^\circ$.
Step 2: N-Ethyl-N-methylpropan-2-amine is $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CH-N(CH_3)(C_2H_5)}$: N carries isopropyl, ethyl and methyl groups, so it is $3^\circ$.
Final Answer: (D) N-Ethyl-N-Methylpropan-2-amine
Quick Tip: Two N-prefixes (N,N-disubstituted) on an alkanamine name means a tertiary amine.

questions.stem: Which of the following aqueous solutions having same molality exhibits maximum boiling point elevation? (Assume complete dissociation)
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\Delta T_b = i K_b m$; at equal molality the largest van't Hoff factor $i$ gives the largest elevation.
Step 2: KCl and NaCl give 2 ions ($i = 2$), $\mathrm{BaCl_2}$ gives 3 ($i = 3$), $\mathrm{AlCl_3 \rightarrow Al^{3+} + 3Cl^-}$ gives 4 ($i = 4$).
Final Answer: (C) $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$
Quick Tip: Colligative properties depend on the number of particles, so count ions per formula unit.

questions.stem: Identify the monomers used in preparation of dacron.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Dacron (terylene) is a polyester formed by condensation of ethylene glycol and terephthalic acid (benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid).
Step 2: $\mathrm{n\,HO-CH_2CH_2-OH + n\,HOOC-C_6H_4-COOH \rightarrow [-OCH_2CH_2O-CO-C_6H_4-CO-]_n + 2n\,H_2O}$; option (C) shows exactly these two monomers.
Final Answer: (C) $\mathrm{HO(CH_2)_2-OH}$ and terephthalic acid
Quick Tip: (A) gives bakelite, (B) gives Buna-N; Dacron = glycol + terephthalic acid.

questions.stem: Identify least stable species from following.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Alkyl groups have a +I (electron-releasing) effect that disperses the positive charge on nitrogen and stabilises the ammonium ion.
Step 2: $\mathrm{NH_4^+}$ has no alkyl group, so its positive charge is not dispersed at all; on the basis of the inductive effect it is the least stable (stability $\mathrm{R_3NH^+ > R_2NH_2^+ > RNH_3^+ > NH_4^+}$).
Final Answer: (A) $\mathrm{NH_4^{+}}$
Quick Tip: This is why alkylamines are stronger bases than ammonia: their conjugate acids are more stable.

questions.stem: Which instrument is used for determination of particle size?
questions.solution:
Step 1: In the transmission electron microscope (TEM) the electron beam passes through the sample, giving a high-resolution image from which the size (and shape) of individual nanoparticles is measured.
Step 2: SEM mainly gives surface morphology, FTIR identifies functional groups and UV-visible spectroscopy gives optical properties.
Final Answer: (B) TEM
Quick Tip: TEM - particle size; SEM - surface; XRD - crystal structure; FTIR - bonds; UV-Vis - optical absorption.

questions.stem:
Identify ' $A$ ' in the following reaction.
$\mathrm{A}$ + chloromethane $\xrightarrow[\mathrm{AlCl_3}]{\text{Anhydrous}}$ 2-chlorotoluene + 4-chlorotoluene
questions.solution:
Step 1: Chloromethane with anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$ is a Friedel-Crafts methylation; it adds a $\mathrm{-CH_3}$ group to the ring.
Step 2: The products are chlorotoluenes, so the ring already had Cl: A is chlorobenzene. Cl is o,p-directing, so $\mathrm{C_6H_5Cl + CH_3Cl \xrightarrow{anhyd.\ AlCl_3} o\text{-}ClC_6H_4CH_3 + p\text{-}ClC_6H_4CH_3 + HCl}$.
Final Answer: (B) Chlorobenzene
Quick Tip: Halogens deactivate the ring but still direct incoming groups to ortho and para positions.

questions.stem: What is the average rate of reaction when change in concentration of product is 0.05 M in 20 seconds?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Average rate $= \frac{\Delta[\text{P}]}{\Delta t}$
Step 2: $= \frac{0.05\ \mathrm{M}}{20\ \mathrm{s}} = 0.0025\ \mathrm{M\,s^{-1}}$
Final Answer: (A) $0.0025\ \mathrm{M\,s^{-1}}$
Quick Tip: Rate = concentration change / time; 20/0.05 = 400 would be the inverse trap.

questions.stem: Identify the product ' $A$ ' in the following reaction, Anisole $\xrightarrow[398\ \mathrm{K}]{\mathrm{HI}}$ $\mathrm{A}$ + Iodomethane
questions.solution:
Step 1: HI cleaves alkyl aryl ethers at the $\mathrm{O-CH_3}$ bond, because the $\mathrm{O-C_6H_5}$ bond has partial double bond character and $\mathrm{I^-}$ attacks the methyl carbon ($S_N2$).
Step 2: $\mathrm{C_6H_5OCH_3 + HI \xrightarrow{398\ K} C_6H_5OH + CH_3I}$, so A is phenol (benzenol).
Final Answer: (C) Benzenol
Quick Tip: Anisole + HI never gives iodobenzene; the aryl-oxygen bond is not broken.

questions.stem: \"Pairing of electrons in the orbitals belonging to the same subshell does not occur unless each orbital belonging to that subshell has got one electron each.\" This statement is known as
questions.solution:
Step 1: Hund's rule of maximum multiplicity says degenerate orbitals are first singly occupied with parallel spins, and pairing starts only after each has one electron.
Step 2: Pauli's principle limits an orbital to two electrons of opposite spin, and Aufbau gives the order of filling - neither describes this statement.
Final Answer: (B) Hund's rule
Quick Tip: e.g. N is $2p_x^{1}2p_y^{1}2p_z^{1}$, not $2p_x^{2}2p_y^{1}$ - that is Hund's rule.

questions.stem: What is oxidation state of xenon in xenonmonooxytetrafluoride?
questions.solution:
Step 1: The compound is $\mathrm{XeOF_4}$. Let O.N. of Xe be $x$, with O $= -2$ and F $= -1$.
Step 2: $x + (-2) + 4(-1) = 0$, so $x = +6$
Final Answer: (C) +6
Quick Tip: $\mathrm{XeOF_4}$ is formed by partial hydrolysis of $\mathrm{XeF_6}$, so Xe keeps the +6 state.

questions.stem: Calculate the mole fraction of pure liquid $B$ in solution if total vapour pressure of solution, vapour pressure of pure liquid A and vapour pressure of pure liquid B are 500 mm Hg , 400 mm Hg and 575 mm Hg respectively at given temperature.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Raoult's law: $P = P_A^{0}x_A + P_B^{0}x_B = P_A^{0} + (P_B^{0} - P_A^{0})x_B$
Step 2: $500 = 400 + (575 - 400)x_B = 400 + 175\,x_B$
Step 3: $x_B = \frac{100}{175} = 0.571 \approx 0.57$
Final Answer: (B) 0.57
Quick Tip: Write $x_A = 1 - x_B$ so that only one unknown remains.

questions.stem: What happens to the emf for the cell, $\mathrm{Zn_{(s)} \left| Zn^{+2}_{(1M)} \right\| Ag^{+1}(1M) \left| Ag_{(s)} \right.}$ if concentration of $\mathrm{Ag^{+1}}$ decreases to 0.1 M ?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Cell reaction $\mathrm{Zn + 2Ag^+ \rightarrow Zn^{2+} + 2Ag}$, $n = 2$; $E = E^\circ - \frac{0.0592}{2}\log\frac{[\mathrm{Zn^{2+}}]}{[\mathrm{Ag^+}]^{2}}$
Step 2: Initially $[\mathrm{Ag^+}] = 1$ M, so $E = E^\circ$. With $[\mathrm{Ag^+}] = 0.1$ M: $E = E^\circ - \frac{0.0592}{2}\log\frac{1}{(0.1)^{2}} = E^\circ - \frac{0.0592}{2} \times 2$
Step 3: $E = E^\circ - 0.0592\ \mathrm{V}$, i.e. the emf decreases by 0.0592 V
Final Answer: (B) decrease by 0.0592 V
Quick Tip: Lowering the concentration of a reactant (here the cathode ion) always lowers the cell emf.

questions.stem: The attractive interactions between cations and mobile electrons in metallic solid is called
questions.solution:
Step 1: In a metal, positive ions (kernels) sit in a 'sea' of delocalised valence electrons.
Step 2: The electrostatic attraction between these cations and the mobile electrons holds the solid together and is called the metallic bond.
Final Answer: (D) metallic bond
Quick Tip: Mobile electrons explain the electrical and thermal conductivity of metals.

questions.stem: Identify weak field ligand from following.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Spectrochemical series: $\mathrm{I^- < Br^- < SCN^- < Cl^- < F^- < OH^- < H_2O < NH_3 < en < CN^- < CO}$.
Step 2: Halide ions are at the weak-field end (small $\Delta_o$); $\mathrm{NH_3}$ is moderate-to-strong and $\mathrm{CN^-}$, CO are strong field. So $\mathrm{Br^-}$ is the weak field ligand.
Final Answer: (C) $\mathrm{Br^{-}}$
Quick Tip: Halides are weak field, $\mathrm{CN^-}$ and CO are strong field ($\pi$-acceptors).

questions.stem: What is the value of spin only magnetic moment for $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ in BM?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Cu ($Z = 29$): $\mathrm{[Ar]}\,3d^{10}4s^{1}$; $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$: $\mathrm{[Ar]}\,3d^{9}$, so $n = 1$ unpaired electron.
Step 2: $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} = \sqrt{1 \times 3} = \sqrt{3}$
Step 3: $\mu = 1.73\ \mathrm{BM}$
Final Answer: (C) 1.73
Quick Tip: $n$ = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 gives $\mu$ = 1.73, 2.83, 3.87, 4.90, 5.92 BM.

questions.stem:
Identify role of glycerol in following reaction.
$\mathrm{2H_2O_{2(\ell)} \xrightarrow{glycerol} 2H_2O_{(\ell)} + O_{2(g)}}$
questions.solution:
Step 1: Glycerol slows down the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide; it is added to $\mathrm{H_2O_2}$ solutions to stabilise them.
Step 2: A substance that decreases the rate of a reaction is a negative catalyst, i.e. an inhibitor.
Final Answer: (B) Inhibitor
Quick Tip: Glycerol, acetanilide and phosphoric acid are classic inhibitors for $\mathrm{H_2O_2}$ decomposition.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a Fittig reaction?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Fittig reaction: two aryl halide molecules couple with sodium in dry ether to give a biaryl.
Step 2: $\mathrm{2C_6H_5Br + 2Na \xrightarrow{dry\ ether} C_6H_5-C_6H_5 + 2NaBr}$ (biphenyl). (A) is Wurtz-Fittig (aryl + alkyl), (B) and (C) are Wurtz (alkyl + alkyl).
Final Answer: (D) $\mathrm{2C_6H_5Br + 2Na \xrightarrow[ether]{dry} C_6H_5-C_6H_5 + 2NaBr}$
Quick Tip: Wurtz = alkyl + alkyl; Fittig = aryl + aryl; Wurtz-Fittig = aryl + alkyl.

questions.stem: The slope of a graph $\log[A]_t$ versus ' $t$ ' for first order reaction is $-2.5 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$. Find rate constant of the reaction?
questions.solution:
Step 1: For a first order reaction $\log[A]_t = \log[A]_0 - \frac{k}{2.303}t$, so slope $= -\frac{k}{2.303}$
Step 2: $-\frac{k}{2.303} = -2.5 \times 10^{-3}$, so $k = 2.303 \times 2.5 \times 10^{-3}$
Step 3: $k = 5.757 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$
Final Answer: (C) $5.757 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$
Quick Tip: Slope of $\ln[A]$ vs $t$ is $-k$; slope of $\log[A]$ vs $t$ is $-k/2.303$.

questions.stem:
Identify the product formed in the following reaction.
$\mathrm{CH_3CH_2MgBr} \xrightarrow[\text{ii) dil. HCl}]{\text{i) Dry ice/ dry ether}}$ Product
questions.solution:
Step 1: Grignard reagent adds to $\mathrm{CO_2}$ (dry ice): $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2MgBr + CO_2 \rightarrow CH_3CH_2COOMgBr}$
Step 2: Acid hydrolysis: $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COOMgBr + H_2O \xrightarrow{H^+} CH_3CH_2COOH + Mg(OH)Br}$, i.e. propanoic acid.
Final Answer: (B) Propanoic acid
Quick Tip: $\mathrm{RMgX + CO_2}$ then $\mathrm{H_3O^+}$ gives $\mathrm{RCOOH}$ with one more carbon than R.

questions.stem: What is pH of weak dibasic acid, that is $2\%$ dissociated in its M/100 solution at 298 K ?
questions.solution:
Step 1: $c = 0.01\ \mathrm{M}$, $\alpha = 0.02$. A dibasic acid $\mathrm{H_2A}$ releases 2 $\mathrm{H^+}$ per dissociated molecule, so $[\mathrm{H^+}] = 2c\alpha$.
Step 2: $[\mathrm{H^+}] = 2 \times 0.01 \times 0.02 = 4 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{M}$
Step 3: $\mathrm{pH} = -\log(4 \times 10^{-4}) = 4 - 0.602 = 3.398 \approx 3.3970$
Final Answer: (C) 3.3970
Quick Tip: For a dibasic acid count two $\mathrm{H^+}$ per dissociated molecule; ignoring this gives pH 3.699 (not an option).

questions.stem: Identify from following the correct set of thermodynamic conditions for the reaction to be spontaneous at all temperatures.
questions.solution:
Step 1: A reaction is spontaneous when $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S < 0$.
Step 2: If $\Delta H < 0$ and $\Delta S > 0$, both terms make $\Delta G$ negative ($-T\Delta S$ is negative), so $\Delta G < 0$ at every temperature.
Final Answer: (C) $\Delta \mathrm{H} < 0$ and $\Delta \mathrm{S} > 0$
Quick Tip: (A) is spontaneous only at high T, (B) only at low T, (D) never.

questions.stem:
Which of the following net cell reaction takes place in a galvanic cell containing copper electrode and standard hydrogen electrode?
$\mathrm{E^{o}\left(Cu^{+2}_{(aq)} \mid Cu_{(s)}\right) = +0.34\ V}$
questions.solution:
Step 1: $E^\circ(\mathrm{Cu^{2+}/Cu}) = +0.34$ V is higher than $E^\circ(\mathrm{H^+/H_2}) = 0$, so Cu is the cathode (reduction) and the SHE is the anode (oxidation).
Step 2: Anode: $\mathrm{H_2 \rightarrow 2H^+ + 2e^-}$; cathode: $\mathrm{Cu^{2+} + 2e^- \rightarrow Cu}$. Net: $\mathrm{H_2 + Cu^{2+} \rightarrow 2H^+ + Cu}$, $E^\circ_{cell} = +0.34$ V.
Final Answer: (B) $\mathrm{H_{2(g)} + Cu^{+2}_{(aq)} \longrightarrow 2H^{+}_{(aq)} + Cu_{(s)}}$
Quick Tip: In a galvanic cell the electrode with the higher reduction potential is reduced; (C) shows two oxidations and (D) two reductions, so neither can be a cell reaction.

questions.stem: Identify neutral complex from following.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Write the formulas: $\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}$ (anion), $\mathrm{Na_3[AlF_6]}$ (complex anion $\mathrm{[AlF_6]^{3-}}$), $\mathrm{[Cu(NH_3)_4]^{2+}}$ (cation).
Step 2: Triamminetrinitrocobalt(III) is $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_3(NO_2)_3]}$: charge $= +3 + 3(0) + 3(-1) = 0$, a neutral complex (no counter ions and no 'ion' in the name).
Final Answer: (C) Triamminetrinitrocobalt (III)
Quick Tip: A neutral complex's name is a single word with no 'ion' and no separate cation/anion name.

questions.stem: Which from following polymers is used to obtain surgical sutures?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Nylon 6,6 is a polyamide made from hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid: $\mathrm{n\,H_2N(CH_2)_6NH_2 + n\,HOOC(CH_2)_4COOH \rightarrow [-NH(CH_2)_6NH-CO(CH_2)_4CO-]_n + 2n\,H_2O}$.
Step 2: Its fibres have high tensile strength, are smooth, chemically inert and non-toxic, so besides textiles, bristles and ropes it is used to make surgical sutures (as listed in the state-board textbook). Neoprene is a rubber and terylene is a polyester used mainly in fabrics.
Final Answer: (B) Nylon 6,6
Quick Tip: Learn the textbook 'uses' list for each polymer - MHT-CET asks them directly.
